articles.title: 400 km, five districts and two years: The remarkable journey of a young tiger searching for a place to call home
articles.summary: Animals & Pets News: A young tiger has turned into one of Maharashtra’s most unexpected long-distance travellers. The big cat, believed to have originated in Tipeshwar Wil.
articles.body: A young tiger has turned into one of Maharashtra’s most unexpected long-distance travellers. The big cat, believed to have originated in Tipeshwar Wildlife Sanctuary in Yavatmal, has been moving across central Maharashtra for nearly two years. It was recently photographed in Beed, more than 400 km from its original habitat, before disappearing from surveillance for several days.It has now been traced again in neighbouring Dharashiv district.The tiger was not ‘lost’ in the usual senseThe word “missing” can make the story sound like a tiger escaped from a zoo or was being searched for after captivity. That is not what happened here.The animal is wild and has been moving through forests and hilly landscapes on its own. Forest officials had camera traps in place to monitor its movements, but no images were recorded for nearly 10 days after its last confirmed sighting.That gap ended on August 29, when the tiger was traced near Yeswandi in Vashi tehsil of Dharashiv.How its 400-km journey unfoldedThe tiger was first spotted in the Ashti hills of Beed on December 10, 2025. It appeared there again on July 27, 2026.Then came a cattle kill in Brahmagaon on August 13. Following the incident, the forest department increased surveillance and installed camera traps. The tiger was photographed on August 20.After that, there was silence.Nearly 10 days later, officials detected the animal again near Yeswandi. It is now moving along the Terkheda-Yeswandi stretch around the Bhoom and Dharashiv borders.Why did the tiger travel so far?Tigers naturally need large territories, particularly young males looking for suitable areas to establish themselves. But this journey is significant because the animal has crossed several districts while apparently finding enough food and water to continue moving.According to forest officials, the tiger has explored parts of Beed, Latur, Dharashiv, Solapur and Ahilyanagar during the past two years.Its prolonged presence also suggests that parts of this landscape can support a large carnivore. Officials have pointed to the availability of prey and water as important reasons for its continued movement through the region.The forest corridor may be the bigger storyThe tiger’s journey tells a story larger than one wandering animal.Its movement provides evidence that the natural corridor between Tipeshwar and Yedshi Ramling Ghat Wildlife Sanctuary is still functioning. Wildlife corridors allow animals to move between habitats instead of becoming trapped in isolated forest patches.The Yedshi region has now emerged as an important centre of the tiger’s wide-ranging movements. Officials believe it may continue towards Naldurg and Yedshi.As Range Forest Officer Amol Munde said, “The tiger is currently roaming the Terkheda-Yeswandi stretch along the Bhoom and Dharashiv borders and is likely moving towards Naldurg and Yedshi.”For a tiger, a 400-km journey is not simply a remarkable distance. It is a reminder that wildlife does not recognise the boundaries drawn on a map. When forests, water sources and prey remain connected, animals can still find their way across landscapes that humans consider separate.Disclaimer: This article is based on information reported by PTI and statements attributed to Maharashtra forest officials. The tiger’s exact route, age and identity have not been publicly established in the cited report beyond its reported origin from Tipeshwar Wildlife Sanctuary.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Is $155,600 a working-class salary? More and more Americans say yes.
articles.summary: In an age of politicians trying to appeal to the working class, more Americans see themselves as part of those ranks.
articles.body:
More Americans view themselves as working class, especially middle-income earners.

A new survey from Pew finds that workers with a savings net and bills paid still feel working-class.

Political views also affect working-class identity, with Republicans more likely to use the label.

A majority of Americans hear themselves in Dolly Parton's "9-to-5."

Sixty percent of Americans identify as working class, according to a Pew Research analysis of a January 2026 survey. That's up from 54% in 2024.

And the label, historically applied to lower-earning workers, resonates across earnings levels. Middle-income families, who make between $51,900 to $155,600 depending on family size and location, identify especially with the term "working class." More surprisingly, half of high-income families, who earn more than $155,600, identify that way.

That could be because the term itself is ambiguous: As the analysis notes, there's no one clear definition of working class. Some equate the working class with lower earners, while others see them as workers without a bachelor's degree, or those explicitly working in blue-collar fields like construction and agriculture.

The Pew findings come as middle-earning or financially comfortable Americans don't feel well-off, even while their pay has grown. Median weekly earnings increased 8.4% from the first quarter of 2024 through the first quarter of 2026, outpacing the 5.5% inflation in prices over that time.

Do you consider yourself working class? Do you have an opinion on what it would take to get out of the working class? Contact this reporter at jkaplan@businessinsider.com .

The middle third of earners used to feel similarly about their savings and spending as higher-earners did. Those two groups have increasingly drifted apart, with sentiment among the middle earners tracking more closely with the lowest earners. That's reflected in how they're spending, too: In 2024, Morning Consult found that middle-income consumers were spending more like their lower-income counterparts. The increased identification with the working class also dovetails with a shrinking middle class, which has fallen from 61% of the population in 1971 to 51% in 2023.

Some of the growing disconnect might be because of inflation . High prices generally make people feel bad about their economic prospects, and over the past few months, inflation has outpaced wage growth . Financial stress also correlates with identifying as working-class. Even still, half of those who reported a baseline of financial comfort — bills paid, expenses met, months of emergency savings — identified with the term working-class.

Your political leanings might also play a role in working-class identification, especially as affordability messaging takes center stage in America. Steven Shepard, the associate director of political research at Pew and one of the report's authors, said, "If you hold most of these other things equal, that Republicans are just more likely to say that that term describes them than Democrats." Upper-income Republicans are far more likely to see themselves as working class than their Democratic counterparts.

On the other side of the political spectrum, progressive politicians have homed in on this newly expanded working class. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani campaigned on an affordability platform meant to ease costs for the working class, which he told The New York Times is the "one majority in this country."

"If you have to work to pay your bills, I think that that is one definition of being a part of the working class," Mamdani said.

articles.title: 'Bomba atômica', diz imprensa mundial sobre revelações Vorcaro-Moraes | G1
articles.standfirst: Imprensa internacional repercute notícia sobre trocas de mensagens entre banqueiro do Banco Master e número atribuído a ministro do STF.
articles.summary: Imprensa internacional repercute notícia sobre trocas de mensagens entre banqueiro do Banco Master e número atribuído a ministro do STF.
articles.body:
A imprensa internacional repercutiu a notícia sobre as trocas de mensagens entre o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, do Banco Master, e um número atribuído ao ministro Alexandre de Moraes , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ).

Uma troca de mensagens divulgada pelo jornal O Estado de S. Paulo entre Moraes e o dono do Banco Master indica que o ministro discutiu com o banqueiro a possibilidade de a Polícia Federal deflagrar a primeira fase da Operação Compliance Zero e a estratégia que ele deveria adotar para frustrar o cumprimento da ordem de prisão preventiva expedida pela 10.ª Vara Federal do Distrito Federal.

Em 15 de novembro de 2025, dois dias antes de sua prisão, o banqueiro pergunta a Moraes: "Acha que segunda já tenho que estar fora?".

As mensagens obtidas pela investigação também indicam que Vorcaro teria pedido a Moraes que interferisse em seu favor junto ao diretor da PF, Andrei Rodrigues, e ao procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet.

O jornal espanhol El País afirmou que "Moraes permanece em silêncio diante dessas revelações, que caíram como uma bomba atômica a menos de cinco semanas das eleições".

O El País afirma que as primeiras suspeitas de uma relação entre Moraes e Vorcaro já haviam surgido há meses, diante da revelação de que o escritório da esposa de Moraes havia sido contratado pelo banqueiro.

Alexandre de Moraes (à esquerda), ministro do Supremo Tribunal, e Daniel Vorcaro, ex-presidente do Banco Master. — Foto: Getty Images/Banco Master via BBC

"Desde que essas revelações envolveram o juiz mais controverso e internacionalmente conhecido do Brasil, ele tem mantido um perfil discreto", afirma o jornal espanhol.

O El País também destaca que o ministro André Mendonça — que liberou o sigilo das mensagens — e Moraes "estão envolvidos numa luta silenciosa pelo poder dentro do tribunal há meses".

"As eleições influenciarão o Supremo Tribunal Federal, pois o vencedor terá a oportunidade de nomear juízes para preencher as três vagas que surgirão durante o seu mandato e poderá alterar a maioria, que atualmente favorece Moraes", diz o jornal espanhol.

"O caso Master é uma trama complexa que também envolve diretamente o candidato presidencial Flávio Bolsonaro, já que o banqueiro preso teria lhe dado US$ 10 milhões, supostamente para financiar uma cinebiografia sobre seu pai."

O caso também repercutiu entre jornais argentinos.

"Um terremoto político e institucional está abalando os alicerces do Supremo Tribunal Federal do Brasil", afirma o jornal La Nacion.

" Alexandre de Moraes , considerado o juiz mais poderoso do país e relator do julgamento da tentativa de golpe de 2023, viu-se no centro de um escândalo sem precedentes na terça-feira, após surgirem evidências de uma relação excessivamente próxima com o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, que está preso e sendo investigado por fraudes financeiras multimilionárias envolvendo o extinto Banco Master."

O La Nacion afirma que, para a política brasileira, o impacto das revelações "é sísmico devido ao próprio peso de Moraes".

"Com o caso nas mãos do plenário, o homem que personificou a Suprema Corte do Brasil se prepara para enfrentar o teste mais difícil contra o seu próprio gabinete."

O jornal argentino Clarin destacou o impacto que as revelações podem ter nas eleições presidenciais do próximo mês.

"Esses novos indícios são revelados em meio à campanha eleitoral para as eleições presidenciais de 4 de outubro, que se configuram como uma disputa direta entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro."

A agência de notícias para o mercado financeiro Bloomberg destacou que novos vazamentos envolveram Moraes ainda mais no escândalo do Banco Master.

"Os documentos [revelados] colocaram Moraes novamente no centro de um caso que já havia ameaçado a credibilidade da mais alta corte do Brasil — uma instituição poderosa da qual ele frequentemente tem sido um símbolo", afirma reportagem da Bloomberg.

"Eles também levaram os opositores do magistrado — que ganhou destaque durante embates com o bilionário da tecnologia Elon Musk e com o ex-presidente de direita Jair Bolsonaro — a renovar os pedidos por seu afastamento do tribunal."

"Moraes é uma figura que divide opiniões no Brasil, onde despertou a ira de conservadores que o acusaram de censura durante uma cruzada contra as chamadas 'fake news' nas redes sociais. Ele desempenhou um papel central no julgamento que condenou Bolsonaro sob a acusação de tramar um golpe após sua derrota nas eleições de 2022 para o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva."

articles.title: Adolescente morto em Petrolina: crime ocorreu no bairro São Gonçalo | G1
articles.standfirst: Guilherme da Conceição Araújo foi atingido por disparos na noite de terça-feira (1º). Suspeito fugiu de moto e a polícia vai analisar imagens de câmeras de segurança.
articles.summary: Guilherme da Conceição Araújo foi atingido por disparos e o autor fugiu de moto; câmeras de segurança podem ajudar a identificar o atirador no Sertão.
articles.body:
IML Petrolina — Foto: Emerson Rocha / g1 Petrolina

Um adolescente de 15 anos foi morto a tiros na noite de terça-feira (1º), na Avenida Tapuio, no bairro São Gonçalo, em Petrolina , no Sertão de Pernambuco. A vítima foi identificada como Guilherme da Conceição Araújo. O autor chegou ao local em uma motocicleta e fugiu após cometer o crime.

O Instituto de Criminalística fez a perícia no local do crime. Após a conclusão dos trabalhos, o corpo foi encaminhado ao Instituto de Medicina Legal (IML) de Petrolina.

Durante as diligências, foram identificadas câmeras de segurança nas proximidades. As imagens serão analisadas pela equipe policial e poderão contribuir para a reconstrução da dinâmica do crime e para a identificação do atirador.

A investigação está sob responsabilidade da 25ª Delegacia de Polícia de Homicídios de Petrolina, que continuará realizando buscas para esclarecer a autoria e a motivação do assassinato.

articles.title: Rogério Valença: companheiro homenageia ex-cantor da Calcinha Preta | G1
articles.standfirst: Ex-vocalista da banda Calcinha Preta morreu aos 55 anos em Sergipe enquanto aguardava por um transplante de rim.
articles.summary: Rogério Valença, ex-vocalista da Calcinha Preta, recebeu homenagem do companheiro após falecer aos 55 anos em Sergipe enquanto aguardava transplante de rim.
articles.body:
Companheiro de Rogério Valença faz homenagem ao cantor nas redes sociais — Foto: Reprodução/ Redes sociais

O esposo do cantor Rogério Valença publicou uma homenagem ao artista em suas redes sociais. Ex-vocalista da banda Calcinha Preta, o músico morreu aos 55 anos, nesta segunda-feira (31), em Aracaju .

Na publicação, o companheiro, com quem o cantor estava casado há mais de 20 anos, compartilhou uma imagem gravada por ele e escreveu:

“Essa foto fui eu que tirei...sem imaginar que guardaria para sempre um pedacinho de você. Que todos se lembrem de você assim: cheio de luz, sabedoria, risadas e alegria. Hoje você contempla o céu de outro lugar, mas continua brilhando em nossos corações”.

Rogério Valença tratava uma insuficiência renal e aguardava por um transplante de rim, mas morreu após sofrer um infarto.

Natural de Garanhuns (PE), o cantor integrou as bandas Calcinha Preta e Caviar com Rapadura. Atualmente, ele morava em Sergipe e se apresentava no grupo Raio da Silibrina.

O velório foi realizado na capital sergipana e o corpo do artista levado para ser sepultado em sua cidade natal.

articles.title: Homem passa mal na fila de mutirão de catarata em UBS de Teresina | G1
articles.standfirst: Paciente precisou ser atendido pelo Samu na manhã desta quarta-feira (2), na UBS Parque Piauí. FMS informou que houve atraso no início dos atendimentos.
articles.summary: Paciente precisou ser atendido pelo Samu na manhã desta quarta-feira (2), na UBS Parque Piauí. FMS informou que houve atraso no início dos atendimentos.
articles.body:
Um homem que aguardava atendimento no mutirão de catarata da Unidade Básica de Saúde (UBS) do Parque Piauí , na Zona Sul de Teresina , passou mal e precisou ser atendido pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) na manhã desta quarta-feira (2). Pacientes que estavam na unidade também relataram desorganização e demora para o início da triagem.

Em nota, a Fundação Municipal de Saúde (FMS) informou que houve um atraso no início dos atendimentos do mutirão nesta quarta-feira (2). Segundo o órgão, o problema ocorreu devido a um atraso pontual da equipe do HVisão, responsável pelos atendimentos .

O radialista Jessé Machado Souza, de 56 anos, que pretendia passar pela triagem, relatou ao g1 que os computadores para o atendimento ainda estavam sendo instalados no momento em que os pacientes aguardavam na unidade.

Segundo Jessé, havia pessoas reclamando na portaria e as senhas ainda não tinham sido distribuídas. Ele também avaliou que houve falhas de planejamento e organização para a realização da ação.

"Está uma bagunça generalizada. Eles estão montando os computadores de atendimento agora, nesse exato momento. O pessoal está aqui reclamando, aqui na portaria. Nem as senhas foram entregues para os atendimentos", relatou.

Homem passa mal esperando por atendimento para mutirão de catarata em Teresina; pacientes denunciam desorganização — Foto: Reprodução

O mutirão de catarata oferece 1,4 mil vagas para triagem de pacientes pelo SUS em Teresina. A ação começou na segunda-feira (31) e segue até esta quinta-feira (3), com 350 vagas por dia.

Nesta quarta-feira, a triagem acontece na UBS Parque Piauí. Podem participar pessoas com mais de 55 anos com suspeita de catarata, além de pacientes que já têm diagnóstico e aguardam cirurgia ou exames pré-operatórios.

Para participar, o paciente deve procurar uma UBS de Teresina para realizar o agendamento, levando documento com foto e CPF.

Segundo a organização do mutirão, durante a triagem é feita a avaliação oftalmológica e, caso haja indicação para cirurgia, o procedimento pode ser agendado no mesmo dia. Os exames pré-operatórios também são realizados durante o atendimento.

A Fundação Municipal de Saúde (FMS) informa que, especificamente nesta quarta-feira (2), houve um pequeno atraso no início dos atendimentos do mutirão de catarata na UBS Parque Piauí, em razão de um atraso pontual da equipe do HVisão, responsável pela realização dos atendimentos.

A FMS esclarece que a situação já está sendo regularizada e que todos os pacientes que aguardam na unidade serão atendidos. Para garantir maior organização do fluxo, estão sendo distribuídas senhas aos pacientes que aguardam pelo atendimento.

A Fundação informa ainda que, ao longo desta semana, a UBS Parque Piauí passou por uma série de ações de organização e preparação para receber a população durante o mutirão, incluindo troca de forro, limpeza terminal e demais adequações necessárias para garantir melhores condições de atendimento.

articles.title: Aposentadoria PcD: regra do INSS pode permitir benefício mais vantajoso | G1
articles.standfirst: Pouco conhecida, aposentadoria da pessoa com deficiência pode permitir menos tempo de contribuição e cálculo mais favorável, conforme cada caso
articles.summary: Pouco conhecida, aposentadoria da pessoa com deficiência pode permitir menos tempo de contribuição e cálculo mais favorável, conforme cada caso
articles.body:
Muitas pessoas passam anos contribuindo para o INSS sem saber que podem se enquadrar nas regras específicas da aposentadoria da pessoa com deficiência.

Isso acontece, muitas vezes, porque ainda existe uma visão limitada sobre o que significa, juridicamente, ser uma pessoa com deficiência.

Escritório Vanessa Alves Advocacia — Foto: Divulgação

Para fins previdenciários, a análise não se limita ao nome de uma doença ou à aparência da pessoa. É necessário avaliar se existe um impedimento de longo prazo de natureza física, mental, intelectual ou sensorial que, em interação com barreiras, prejudique a participação plena e efetiva na sociedade.

Vídeo: Escritório Vanessa Alves Advocacia/ Divulgação

Por isso, pessoas que nunca se consideraram pessoas com deficiência podem, em determinadas situações, preencher os critérios legais.

Algumas condições de saúde podem resultar em deficiência

Não existe uma lista fechada de doenças que garanta esse tipo de aposentadoria. O diagnóstico, sozinho, não determina o enquadramento.

Dependendo das limitações e dos impedimentos produzidos ao longo do tempo, condições físicas ou mentais podem ser analisadas sob a perspectiva jurídica da deficiência.

Isso pode ocorrer, por exemplo, em situações envolvendo transtornos mentais persistentes, doenças cardíacas com repercussões funcionais importantes, transplante renal e limitações decorrentes de doenças crônicas.

Isso não significa, porém, que toda pessoa com determinada condição será automaticamente considerada pessoa com deficiência. A análise é individual.

“O ponto mais importante é deixar de perguntar apenas ‘qual doença essa pessoa tem?’ e começar a analisar quais impedimentos essa condição produz, há quanto tempo eles existem e quais barreiras essa pessoa enfrenta no dia a dia. É aí que o conceito jurídico de deficiência começa a aparecer”, explica a advogada previdenciarista Vanessa Alves, do escritório Vanessa Alves Advocacia.

É possível trabalhar e ser considerada pessoa com deficiência

Outro equívoco comum é acreditar que a pessoa precisa estar incapaz para trabalhar. Não precisa.

A aposentadoria da pessoa com deficiência é diferente da aposentadoria por incapacidade permanente. Uma pessoa pode trabalhar, exercer sua profissão e contribuir regularmente para o INSS e, ainda assim, ser considerada pessoa com deficiência para fins previdenciários, desde que preenchidos os requisitos legais.

“Esse é um dos pontos que mais surpreendem. A pessoa muitas vezes diz: ‘mas eu sempre trabalhei’. E isso não exclui, por si só, a deficiência. O que precisa ser analisado é a trajetória daquela pessoa, os impedimentos existentes e as barreiras enfrentadas ao longo do tempo”, explica Vanessa.

A legislação prevê aposentadoria da pessoa com deficiência por tempo de contribuição e por idade.

Na modalidade por tempo de contribuição, o período exigido varia conforme o grau da deficiência:

Deficiência grave: 20 anos de contribuição para mulheres e 25 para homens;

Deficiência moderada: 24 anos para mulheres e 29 para homens;

Deficiência leve: 28 anos para mulheres e 33 para homens.

Nessa modalidade, não há idade mínima, desde que os demais requisitos sejam preenchidos.

Já a aposentadoria por idade exige, atualmente, 55 anos para mulheres e 60 para homens, além de, no mínimo, 15 anos de contribuição cumpridos na condição de pessoa com deficiência e da carência exigida.

Por isso, antes de falar em aposentadoria PcD, é importante identificar qual modalidade pode ser aplicável a cada caso.

A história da deficiência também é analisada

Na aposentadoria por tempo de contribuição, não basta identificar que existe uma deficiência atualmente. A análise também precisa verificar o período em que a condição esteve presente e, quando necessário, seu grau ao longo do tempo.

O reconhecimento é realizado por avaliação própria do INSS, considerando aspectos médicos e funcionais. Isso é especialmente importante quando a pessoa começou a trabalhar antes do surgimento da deficiência ou teve alteração do grau ao longo da vida contributiva.

Outro diferencial está na forma de cálculo. Na aposentadoria por tempo de contribuição da pessoa com deficiência, a Lei Complementar nº 142/2013 prevê renda mensal correspondente a 100% do salário de benefício. O fator previdenciário só é aplicado se resultar em valor mais alto para o segurado.

“Em alguns casos, a pessoa pode descobrir que existe uma regra específica para sua condição que permite antecipar a aposentadoria e alcançar um cálculo mais favorável. Mas isso depende de uma análise completa da vida contributiva e da deficiência”, explica Vanessa Alves.

As regras específicas também permaneceram aplicáveis após a Reforma da Previdência, o que torna essa modalidade relevante diante das mudanças ocorridas nas aposentadorias comuns.

Documentos antigos podem fazer diferença

Um dos maiores desafios pode ser reconstruir a história da deficiência. Em muitos casos, a pessoa convive com determinada condição há anos, mas nunca buscou um reconhecimento formal como pessoa com deficiência. Quando chega o momento de analisar a aposentadoria, surge uma questão importante: desde quando aquela condição pode ser reconhecida para fins previdenciários?

Prontuários médicos, exames, relatórios de tratamento, documentos escolares, registros de afastamentos e outros documentos podem ajudar a reconstruir essa trajetória.

“Às vezes a pessoa tem um documento de quinze ou vinte anos atrás que nunca imaginou que teria importância. Na análise previdenciária, aquele registro pode ajudar a compreender quando determinadas limitações já estavam presentes”, observa Vanessa Alves.

Por isso, antes de pedir a aposentadoria, é importante analisar não apenas o tempo de contribuição, mas também a história de saúde, os períodos em que existiram impedimentos e a possibilidade de aplicação das regras destinadas à pessoa com deficiência.

Advogada responsável - Vanessa Alves, OAB-SP 364848.

articles.title: Negociador do Irã chama EUA de 'Satã' após ataque contra casamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Festa de casamento foi atingida no sul do território iraniano durante um bombardeio norte-americano contra alvos na região do Estreito de Ormuz, segundo autoridades locais.
articles.summary: Festa de casamento foi atingida no sul do território iraniano durante um bombardeio norte-americano contra alvos na região do Estreito de Ormuz, segundo autoridades locais.
articles.body:
O principal negociador iraniano, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, chamou os Estados Unidos de "Satã" após um ataque contra uma festa de casamento no sul do país.

"Escola de Minab: crianças massacradas. Ginásio de Lamerd: crianças assassinadas. Casamento em Kuhestak: crianças assassinadas ao lado de suas famílias. Se uma potência atua como Satã, escolhe alvos como Satã e mata como Satã, é Satã", afirmou Ghalibaf em uma publicação na rede social X.

Segundo o Crescente Vermelho iraniano —braço oriental da Cruz Vermelha—, cinco pessoas, incluindo uma criança, morreram durante um casamento em consequência de um ataque americano no sul do país na terça-feira. Quase 50 ficaram feridas.

"Após um ataque com mísseis dos Estados Unidos , estilhaços atingiram uma residência na cidade de Kuhestak, no distrito de Sirik, onde era celebrado um casamento", escreveu a organização na rede social X.

Os novos ataques americanos começaram pouco após o presidente iraniano, Masoud Pezeshkian, pedir um retorno ao caminho diplomático, atualmente estagnado.

articles.body: US Vice President JD Vance said in a podcast released Tuesday (local time) that he feared a “real civil strife” had a 2024 attempt on Donald Trump’s life been successful.Vance made the remarks during a conversation with Christian podcaster Bryce Crawford. During the conversation, he cited the July 13, 2024, assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania, during which a bullet whizzed past Trump’s ear before striking a supporter, who was killed. The gunman, Thomas Matthew Crooks, was shot dead by Secret Service snipers.“We would have had real civil strife in a way that I don't know that the country could have ever come back from. There would have just been an illegitimacy to our entire political system,” the Associated Press quoted the vice president as saying.Vance further stated that, like many other Trump supporters, he too would have suspected a conspiracy had Crooks been successful.“I would have assumed very dark forces had taken out Donald Trump, right as he was about to come back into the White House. Many Trump supporters would have assumed a conspiracy had robbed them of their chosen president... I would have also had those thoughts 'in the back of my mind,'” he added.On July 15, 2024, Trump formally announced Vance as his running mate, or vice presidential candidate. In the November 2024 election, the Trump-Vance Republican ticket defeated the Democratic ticket of Kamala Harris and her running mate, Tim Walz.Vance on Trump's AI-generated image as Jesus ChristCrawford also asked Vance about a social media post Trump shared earlier this year featuring an AI-generated image of himself as Jesus, which the podcast host described as offensive. Trump initially contended that he thought the image depicted him as a doctor, but later removed the post amid widespread criticism, including from some of his own supporters.Vance defended the president, arguing that Trump did not intend to “mock or mimic God” and that “that's just not who he is.” He added that Trump often tries to keep things light and frequently jokes. “He's a bit of a ballbuster, for those of us who work with him, and he just likes to have a good time,” Vance remarked. “And I think that if people appreciated that, they would recognize, he's not trying to offend people, he's trying to keep things light.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Times Square stabbing: Bank of America VP Erin Piacenti among victims
articles.summary: US News: A 32-year-old vice-president at Bank of America was killed in a stabbing incident in New York’s Times Square. The attack, described by police as “rand.
articles.body: A 32-year-old vice-president at Bank of America was killed in a stabbing incident in New York’s Times Square. The attack, described by police as “random” and unprovoked, unfolded on Monday afternoon.The victim was identified as Erin Piacenti, who was walking home from work when she was attacked near West 42nd Street and Seventh Avenue. Piacenti had recently returned to work after becoming a mother and had shared a photo of herself with her newborn daughter and husband four days before the stabbing.A 68-year-old man was also stabbed in the attack and was in stable condition, according to police. The attacker, identified as 49-year-old Pamela Cisneros, was shot and killed by officers after she advanced towards them while carrying two large knives.Who was Erin Piacenti?Piacenti was a vice-president in Bank of America’s Business Selection and Conflicts unit and had joined the company around 18 months ago, according to an internal memo and her LinkedIn profile.Matthew Koder, Bank of America’s president of Global Corporate & Investment Banking, described Piacenti as a “cherished teammate and friend” in an internal memo.“Erin was a valued member of the Business Selection and Conflicts team, having joined the bank 18 months ago,” Koder wrote. “Her loss is being felt deeply by many.”Bank of America confirmed Piacenti’s death and expressed condolences to her family.“We are shocked and deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague. She was a valued teammate who will be greatly missed. Our hearts go out to her family and all of her loved ones,” the bank said in a statement.Piacenti had earned a law degree from Fordham Law School, graduating in 2021 alongside her husband, Frank, according to the school. Fordham Law said in a statement it was heartbroken by her death.Bank of America’s Manhattan office is located at One Bryant Park, just a few blocks from the site of the stabbing.How the incident unfoldedNYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said the attack appeared to be random and unprovoked. Police identified the attacker as Pamela Cisneros, 49, of Queens.According to Tisch, Cisneros pulled two knives from a shopping bag, stabbed the 68-year-old man and then attacked Piacenti. When officers arrived, they found Cisneros brandishing two large knives and advancing towards them.Officers used a stun gun and tried to persuade her to drop the weapons for several minutes, but she refused. Tisch said Cisneros told officers she “would rather kill” them. Two officers then shot her, and she was later pronounced dead.Tisch said Cisneros had a documented mental health history, with police encounters related to mental health in 2018 and 2019, but no arrest record in New York City.Cisneros’ brother, Patrick Peralta, told Gothamist that she had psychiatric problems for decades but was not aggressive. He said she had been taking medication and had been doing better in recent years, working on and off in a legal office.“We really don’t know how to express or how to explain why this happened," Peralta told Gothamist, expressing sympathy for Piacenti’s family and the injured man.Koder said Bank of America’s security teams were “fully engaged in supporting the police investigation here, and in addressing the ongoing safety and security of our offices and teammates”.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: China News: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong, 29, pleaded guilty on Wednesday to a national security allegation of collusion with foreign entities, an off.
articles.body: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong, 29, pleaded guilty on Wednesday to a national security allegation of collusion with foreign entities, an offence that carries a potential life sentence. Several Western diplomats were present at the hearing.Wong rose to international prominence as a teenage pro-democracy activist, part of a generation of young protesters whose activism has since been effectively criminalised under the sweeping National Security Law that Beijing imposed on Hong Kong in 2020.According to a charge sheet seen by Reuters, prosecutors accused Wong of conspiring with exiled activist Nathan Law and others to solicit foreign countries, institutions, organisations, or individuals to impose sanctions or blockades against Hong Kong and China. The alleged conduct occurred between July 1 and November 23, 2020. Wong was arrested on these charges in June 2025, the second time he has faced prosecution under the National Security Law.During the hearing, prosecutors emphasised an alleged international media and political campaign led by Demosisto, a now-disbanded political party Wong once led, that had advocated for a referendum on Hong Kong's sovereignty. The campaign reportedly sought sanctions against Hong Kong and China in 2019 and 2020.Wong is currently serving a sentence from an earlier national security conviction, conspiracy to commit subversion, stemming from his participation in an unofficial 2020 primary election among democratic activists. That sentence is due to end next year.The National Security Law was enacted on June 30, 2020, partly in response to the often-violent pro-democracy protests that engulfed Hong Kong in 2019.International human rights organisations and Western governments have criticised the law as excessive, arguing it undermines the high degree of autonomy promised to Hong Kong after its 1997 handover from British to Chinese rule.Hong Kong and Chinese authorities, however, maintain the law was necessary to restore stability.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1995, Clint Eastwood sold a large California property for $3.08 million; the land was placed under permanent conservation protection instead of being developed
articles.summary: US News: In 1995, actor and filmmaker Clint Eastwood sold roughly 280 acres of his California coastal property to Monterey County for $3.08 million, helping en.
articles.body: In 1995, actor and filmmaker Clint Eastwood sold roughly 280 acres of his California coastal property to Monterey County for $3.08 million, helping ensure that a large stretch of scenic land would remain undeveloped. The property, associated with Eastwood’s long-held Malpaso holdings near Carmel Highlands, was divided into five parcels and was acquired by the county for open-space preservation. Rather than becoming available for future construction, the land was placed under a conservation easement intended to protect it permanently. The transaction formed part of a wider conservation effort around Carmel and the Carmel River, where several important coastal properties were facing development pressure. Eastwood’s role in the episode was more complicated than a simple donation, since the county purchased the land, but the resulting protection prevented its future development.Clint Eastwood’s long connection to the landEastwood began acquiring property around Malpaso Creek in the late 1960s, building a substantial collection of land along the rugged Monterey County coast. Contemporary accounts reported that his broader holdings in the area eventually covered roughly 650 acres, although the portion involved in the 1995 county transaction was considerably smaller. Eastwood had purchased land in the area during a period when development was increasingly changing parts of the Carmel region, while the coastal landscape around Malpaso Creek retained large areas of undeveloped terrain. The property’s location along Highway 1 and near the Big Sur coast also gave it considerable scenic and environmental importance.The $3.08 million saleIn 1995, Monterey County purchased approximately 279 to 280 acres of Eastwood’s Malpaso property for $3.08 million. The land consisted of five parcels and was acquired for open-space purposes. Contemporary reporting connected the transaction to California’s Proposition 70, a state bond measure that provided money for acquiring and protecting open space. The deal therefore involved a direct purchase rather than a straightforward charitable donation by Eastwood. The distinction matters because the conservation result came through a public acquisition in which the county became the owner of the property.The land was protected from future developmentOne of the most significant aspects of the transaction was what happened after the county acquired the property. The Malpaso land was subject to a conservation easement that required its protection in perpetuity. The restriction was designed to prevent the county’s ownership from later being converted into a development opportunity. The arrangement meant that the property could remain open space rather than being subdivided or built over. Contemporary reporting also noted that the land was not simply turned into a conventional public park, with questions surrounding public access remaining separate from the permanent protection of the property itself.The property had been facing a very different futureThe significance of the acquisition becomes clearer when viewed against the development pressures affecting the Carmel area at the time. Nearby land around the Carmel River was also being considered for residential development, prompting conservation groups and local authorities to look for ways to preserve remaining open spaces. The Malpaso transaction became connected to a broader series of property deals involving the Eastwoods, Monterey County and the Big Sur Land Trust. Together, those efforts helped protect several hundred acres of environmentally and scenically important land around the Carmel coast.The deal was linked to the fight over Odello RanchThe 1995 Malpaso sale was particularly important because it was intertwined with the preservation of the nearby Odello Ranch, a former artichoke-growing property at the mouth of the Carmel River. Development plans had proposed dozens of homes on the approximately 134-acre property. The Eastwoods subsequently became involved in the complicated effort surrounding the site, purchasing the property after a development option was abandoned. The episode eventually helped lead to the preservation of much of the land rather than the residential development originally contemplated.Eastwood later helped protect more coastal landThe conservation story did not end with the Malpaso transaction. In 1997, Eastwood and Maggie Johnson announced an arrangement involving the transfer of substantial Coast Ranch land to the Big Sur Land Trust. Contemporary reports valued the property involved at about $6 million and said the arrangement would keep most of the land from being developed. The deal included restrictions affecting development rights and helped preserve open space around the Carmel River. The preservation effort also involved Monterey County land retained for flood-control purposes and agricultural protections on other portions of the property.The financial side of the Malpaso deal drew scrutinyThe transaction was not without controversy. A later investigation by Coast Weekly examined the financial circumstances surrounding the Malpaso purchase and noted that Monterey County records had placed the property’s assessed value at about $308,682 in July 1994, far below the $3.08 million purchase price. That difference alone does not establish that the county overpaid, since a tax assessment is not necessarily the same as a property’s market value or its value for conservation purposes. However, the disparity became part of the scrutiny surrounding the transaction. The investigation also reported that county officials did not have a record of what Eastwood had originally paid for the property.Conservationists saw both benefits and complicationsThe wider Eastwood land deals generated debate among conservationists and others involved in Monterey County land-use policy. Supporters pointed to the substantial amount of coastal and riverfront land that ultimately escaped development. Critics, meanwhile, questioned the financial and development-rights arrangements involved in the transactions, particularly around Odello Ranch. The debate illustrates that conservation victories involving private landowners and public authorities can involve complicated exchanges of property, development rights, water rights and tax considerations. Even with those disputes, the physical conservation outcome was significant because large areas that had faced development pressure were ultimately placed under long-term protection.Malpaso Creek made the land environmentally significantThe Malpaso property was valuable not only because of its dramatic coastal scenery but also because of its ecological setting. Malpaso Creek runs through the rugged Carmel Highlands landscape before reaching the Pacific, while the surrounding region contains important coastal habitats and Monterey pine forest. Monterey County planning documents have identified the Malpaso area as having significant conservation value, including its importance to Monterey pine habitat. Protecting undeveloped land in this landscape therefore helped preserve more than a scenic backdrop. It also maintained a relatively intact portion of a sensitive coastal environment where development could have fragmented habitat and altered the character of the landscape.It was a sale rather than a celebrity land donationThe distinction between a sale and a donation is central to telling the story accurately. Eastwood did not simply give the roughly 280 acres to Monterey County for free. The county paid $3.08 million to acquire the five parcels, with Proposition 70 funding playing a role in the open-space acquisition. What makes the episode a conservation story is what happened through and after that purchase. The land was acquired for preservation and subjected to a permanent conservation restriction, removing the possibility of ordinary future development.A larger conservation legacy around CarmelThe Malpaso transaction became one part of a broader pattern of land preservation associated with Eastwood’s property interests around Carmel. His involvement with the Mission Ranch, his earlier land transactions in Carmel Valley and the later preservation of land connected to Odello Ranch all contributed to a complicated local history in which privately held property was repeatedly at the centre of debates over development and conservation. The 1995 sale stands out because it converted roughly 280 acres of Eastwood’s coastal holdings into county-owned open space protected by a permanent conservation easement.The strongest legacy of the transaction is therefore not simply that a Hollywood star owned a large piece of California. It is that a substantial portion of his Malpaso property changed hands through a public conservation purchase at a time when development pressure was affecting the Carmel coast. Roughly 279 to 280 acres were sold for $3.08 million and placed under permanent conservation protection, ensuring that the land would not follow the conventional path from private ownership to subdivision and construction. The surrounding transactions were financially and politically complicated, but the central conservation outcome remains clear. A large area of environmentally and scenically important coastal land was secured as protected open space rather than developed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pennsylvania police shooting: Officer charged in death of college student
articles.summary: US News: A Pennsylvania police officer has been charged with voluntary manslaughter after shooting and killing a 22-year-old college student who had wound up a.
articles.body: A Pennsylvania police officer has been charged with voluntary manslaughter after shooting and killing a 22-year-old college student who had wound up at the incorrect residence late at night while waiting for friends to pick him up, stated by the prosecutor on Tuesday.Upper Pottsgrove Police Cpl. Sean Farrell, 58, is accused of Glenwood Earl Pysher IV's death in August 23, according to Montgomery County District Attorney Kevin Steele. The officer did not have to kill Pysher during the confrontation since officer had less-lethal choices, according to the prosecuter.According to a news statement from the district attorney's office, the Montgomery County Detective Bureau looked into the shooting and examined video from Farrell's body-worn camera.According to the inquiry, "Cpl. Farrell had a taser and other less-lethal weapons on his utility belt that he did not use. The victim had his hands raised and was not carrying a weapon at the time of the shot, and the officer was safely behind a vehicle from Pysher. There was no danger from Mr. Pysher. This is not a legal use of deadly force, leading to the charge of Voluntary Manslaughter," as per the news release from Steele.Pysher's family lawyer thanked the prosecution in a statement.Attorney Ken Fulginiti stated, "The family is grateful for the work of the Montgomery County District Attorney's office and they are looking forward to justice in this horribly tragic, preventable, and reckless conduct that took their son's life."On Tuesday, Farrell surrendered to the Montgomery County Detectives. According to a district attorney's office representative, Farrell must surrender all firearms to the state police in order to be released after Magisterial District Judge Kathleen Rebar set bail at $75,000. On September 10, he will have a preliminary hearing.When a resident contacted 911 to report someone attempting to break into a home through the rear door, Farrell was the first officer on the scene. According to the statement, Farrell's body-worn video captured the officer moving down the driveway with his gun drawn and illuminating the path with its light.Farrell noticed Pysher on the patio of the house, close to the back door, while standing behind a car in the driveway. "Police, let me see your hands," shouted Farrell. "Hands up, hands up now, drop to the ground," he then shouted.According to the statement, Pysher was seen on camera raising his hands as he started to approach the officer and kept going in that way as the officer ordered, "Drop to the ground." "Drop to the ground," Farrell yelled once more, followed by "Stop or I'll..." However, according to the district attorney's office, Farrell fired two rounds before he could complete the sentence, striking Pysher twice in the chest.According to the announcement, Pysher was shot between 17 and 20 feet (5 and 6 meters) away from the officer.Pysher had been out at many pubs earlier in the evening to celebrate a friend's 21st birthday, according to the inquiry. Around 11 p.m., a designated driver took the party to the birthday person's house. About 30 minutes later, Pysher exited to walk half a mile to another friend's house to continue drinking, but he ended up at the incorrect residence, according to the release. Based on what his son's friends have told him, Pysher's father has stated that he thinks his son attempted to enter what he believed to be his friend's home.Glen Pysher told The Associated Press last week that "his son tried to open the doorknob and obviously startled the homeowner." According to what we know, he said, "He believed he was at his friend's house, so he said, "Hey! Open the door!"The father said that after his son sat down on the back porch and called his buddies, they noticed he was in the wrong area and started looking for him.Philip Stinson, a criminal justice professor at Bowling Green State University, maintains a national database of almost 25,000 police officer arrests since 2005.Stinson's research shows that between January 2005 and the end of July 2026, 218 local sworn police officers were charged with either murder or manslaughter in a fatal police shot that occurred while they were on duty. Although there are still a number of unresolved cases, 78 policemen have been found guilty, while 107 have been found not guilty or discharged.During that period, ten cops in Pennsylvania were accused, six of them were found guilty.According to Stinson, there have been variations in the number of cops charged over time, but those variations are statistically minor considering that there are about a thousand fatal police confrontations annually."These are ugly situations. "The facts are never simple," Stinson said. Criminal juries and grand juries appear to have similar problems. In a potentially violent street confrontation, they are hesitant to question the split-second, frequently life-or-death judgments made by an on-duty police officer.Most cops involved in deadly on-duty shootings shot an unarmed victim. Just ten of the victims in the 78 convictions had guns when they were shot.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why Greece is betting on Israel’s Achilles Shield
articles.summary: The defence deal between the two countries fits into a larger shift in regional alliances amid the US-Israel war on Iran.
articles.body:
On Monday, Greece and Israel signed a $3.5bn defence deal to build an integrated, multilayered defence network to protect Greek territory dubbed the Achilles Shield. The package brings together the David’s Sling and Spyder interceptors, the Barak air and missile defence system and multimission radars, alongside a separate deal adding Drone Dome systems to protect strategic sites from UAVs.

It is the largest defence deal ever concluded between the two countries. It is also one of the most significant export agreements in Israel’s recent history.

What makes the agreement particularly striking is that it comes as Israel’s global standing is at one of its lowest points in decades. And Greece is no outlier, given that 65 percent of its citizens now view Israel unfavourably. Why, then, has Athens now chosen to openly deepen its ties with Israel in the most politically sensitive of areas: defence and military technology?

Firstly, the shadow of Israel’s conflict with Iran looms large. In early March, an Iranian drone struck Cyprus, Greece’s neighbour and close partner. This likely reinforced anxieties that were already visible in 2024. After Israel, with the help of the United States, downed approximately 300 Iranian drones and missiles, Greek Defence Minister Nikos Dendias called on Athens to develop its own antidrone “dome”.

The deal is therefore partly the product of pragmatic necessity as countries scramble for military solutions to growing drone threats. Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, for example, are acquiring antidrone technology from Ukraine, another country able to market its products as battle-tested.

Despite its political disadvantage, Israel has a practical head start, given that it has long practised “arms diplomacy”, using its defence industry as a springboard to cultivate deeper bilateral ties with prospective buyers.

The second factor driving the Achilles Shield deal is another longstanding tenet of Israeli grand strategy: the “periphery doctrine”. This advocates that Israel develop ties with non-Arab states and peoples on the periphery of the Levant to counter the hostility between Israel and its immediate neighbours. It is a recognition that shared threats can produce strategic partnerships. And in the case of Israel and Greece, that shared threat is Turkiye.

The irony is that Turkiye – as a non-Arab state and the gateway between the Middle East and Europe – was Israel’s close partner in the early days of the periphery doctrine. In 1949, Turkiye was the first Muslim country to recognise Israel. In subsequent years, Ankara and Tel Aviv developed robust but clandestine security ties.

This worked as Israel intended in that it opened the door to increasingly public and broader bilateral relations, which continued even after the Islamist-oriented AK Party, or Justice and Development Party, came to power in Turkiye in 2002.

But both sides fell out in late 2008 after Israel launched an offensive on the Gaza Strip. Subsequent divergences over Israeli policies towards the occupied Palestinian territory have gradually unravelled their deep ties.

Bilateral trade has collapsed since Ankara imposed an embargo on Israel in 2024. There are no longer direct flights between the two countries. In June, US President Donald Trump claimed that US pressure stopped Turkiye from joining the war on Iran, on Tehran’s side. This may sound far-fetched, yet it illustrates how Israel and Turkiye not only disagree on many geopolitical issues, but increasingly see each other as rivals and even threats.

What is remarkable is how quickly Greece has filled the void. In previous years, Tel Aviv’s partnership with Ankara precluded closer ties with Athens. But no more: in late 2025, Israel, Cyprus and Greece signed a “Joint Action Plan” that mandates enhanced military cooperation.

Energy has reinforced this strategic convergence. The discovery of substantial gas reserves in the eastern Mediterranean encouraged Israel, Greece and Cyprus to cooperate on pipelines and maritime security.

And, as was the case with Turkiye, more extensive bilateral ties followed security cooperation: some 744,000 Israelis visited Greece in 2025, compared with the peak of 558,000 Israeli tourists who travelled to Turkiye in 2008.

The increasing regional division into competing blocs has also driven the burgeoning Israel-Greece relationship. In February, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu floated a “ hexagon alliance ” of Israel, Greece, Cyprus, India and unnamed Arab and African countries.

Six months later, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement. This alliance broadly overlaps with what commentators earlier labelled the “Islamic coalition”.

This is an evolving dynamic and inter-bloc collaboration is as common as intra-bloc divergences. But it demonstrates that the crisis of confidence in the US as a security guarantor extends beyond the Gulf states and predates the recent war on Iran. It also portends headaches for Washington’s policymakers, given that these increasingly competing states are all US allies.

The Achilles Shield deal is therefore the new manifestation of an old Israeli strategy that has been accelerated by the US-Israel war on Iran. Public scepticism may complicate Greece-Israel relations, but Israeli-Turkish ties deepened for decades despite similarly unfavourable public attitudes.

In short, in the eastern Mediterranean and elsewhere, growing popular outrage at Israel’s policies will continue to coexist uneasily with deepening security cooperation at an elite level. The irony is that the same conflicts that have damaged Israel’s international standing have also increased the value of its military experience and defence technology.

articles.title: Worshippers in West Bank tear-gassed as Israeli attacks on mosques surge
articles.summary: Palestinian authorities say Israeli forces and settlers have ‘violated’ 13 West Bank mosques this year.
articles.body:
Israeli forces have fired tear gas into a mosque in the occupied West Bank, leaving worshippers inside struggling to breathe, hours after settlers tried to set fire to a second mosque in the territory.

The attacks on Tuesday came as the Palestinian Ministry of Religious Affairs said at least 13 mosques have been “violated” by the Israeli military or settlers since the start of the year.

Footage, verified by Al Jazeera, showed worshippers at the mosque in Madama, near Nablus, coughing in the aftermath of the tear gas attack. One elderly man was seen bent over as another tried to help him.

The ministry said Israeli forces “fired tear gas canisters” into the mosque as people gathered for their evening prayers. The attack “resulted in several elderly worshippers suffering from suffocation and caused widespread disruption to the congregation”, it added.

The attack in Madama came hours after Israeli settlers tried to set fire to another mosque in the nearby town of Bazariya.

Photos and videos from Nur al-Din Zanki Mosque showed blackened burn marks around a window of a room and Hebrew phrases sprayed on the exterior walls.

Majed Nasr, who lives near the mosque, said the attack took place early on Tuesday morning. “There was a small explosion that caused a fire inside the mosque building,” he told the AFP news agency. “We managed to contain the blaze before things could get worse and reach the main upper part of the building.”

The Religious Affairs Ministry condemned the incident as a “criminal attack”.

Local sources told the Anadolu agency that the racist slogans sprayed at the site included threats against Palestinians and a message to the United States ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, saying: “Huckabee, greetings from the terrorists.”

Last month, Huckabee had described Israeli settlers attacking Palestinians in the town of Qusra and other areas of the occupied West Bank as “terrorists”.

The attacks in Madama and Bazariya come as Israeli raids on West Bank mosques have surged following the launch of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza in 2023.

Data from the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED) and Anadolu showed an average of four mosque attacks each year between 2017 and 2022. That figure tripled after the war on Gaza in 2023, with an average of 10 a year. This year’s is the highest annual figure since 2017.

The office of Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas issued a statement following the Madama attack, warning of “the dangers of the continued and escalating religious war” waged by Israeli forces and settlers against religious sites in the occupied West Bank, including the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in occupied East Jerusalem.

The “systematic attacks … crossed all red lines and risked triggering a religious conflict with serious consequences for the region and the world”, it said.

Israeli settlers also burned vehicles in the town of Beta, south of Nablus, and set fire to a Palestinian vehicle in Nahalin, west of Bethlehem, on Tuesday, according to media reports and footage posted online.

The attacks come amid a sharp increase in pogroms by Israeli forces and settlers across the occupied West Bank.

The United Nations said in August that at least 76 Palestinians have been killed in the territory this year and that some 3,800 people have been displaced by settler violence, as well as demolitions and evictions.

It also said settler violence had reached “unprecedented levels,” with more than 1,430 attacks resulting in casualties or property damage documented this year.

Elsewhere in the occupied West Bank on Tuesday, Israeli forces arrested at least 14 Palestinians, including five in Rummanah, one at the Anabta checkpoint, one in Tammun, three in Hebron, two in Bethlehem and two in Nablus.

Israeli forces also uprooted olive trees near Jenin, demolished greenhouses and issued a demolition notice for a home in the town of Idhna.

articles.title: In 1998, Jeopardy! host Alex Trebek donated 74 Hollywood Hills acres worth $2 million, nearly doubling local parkland and protecting trails and a wildlife corridor for deer and coyotes
articles.summary: US News: Alex Trebek is a game show host, most commonly known for Jeopardy!. In 1998, he donated 74 acres of open land in the Hollywood Hills to the Santa Moni.
articles.body: Alex Trebek is a game show host, most commonly known for Jeopardy!. In 1998, he donated 74 acres of open land in the Hollywood Hills to the Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy, with the property valued at $2 million at the time. The donation nearly doubled the public parkland in the area and protected land that officials wanted to preserve as a wildlife corridor.Land next to Runyon CanyonThe property sits north of Hollywood Boulevard and east of Nichols Canyon Road, next to Wattles Park and Runyon Canyon Park. The land already had trails used by hikers and cyclists when Trebek made the donation, according to the Los Angeles Times.John Diaz was the acquisitions director for the Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy at that time, who said that the agency planned to improve those trails after acquiring the property. The land had been sought for more than recreation, however since the conservancy wanted it as a wildlife corridor where deer, coyotes and other animals could move between the Hollywood and San Diego freeways.The property is now Trebek Open SpaceThe land is now known as Trebek Open Space and is managed by the Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority. The agency currently describes it as a 62-acre open space in the Hollywood Hills that adjoins Los Angeles' Runyon Canyon Park. Its existing network of fire roads is used as trails by hikers, mountain bikers and equestrians. The MRCA also identifies the property as land donated by Trebek.The difference between the original 74-acre figure and the current 62-acre description is a reflection of the way the property is documented today. The 1998 newspaper report described the entire parcel donated to the conservancy, while the MRCA's current park listing gives the size of the Trebek Open Space itself as 62 acres.Part of a wider conservation networkThe MRCA manages parks and open-space areas that preserve hillsides, canyons and wildlife habitat within the Los Angeles region. Trebek's property connects with other protected land around Runyon Canyon and Nichols Canyon, which gives hikers access to a landscape that is largely free of buildings despite its location near some of the city's busiest neighborhoods.Instead of treating the 74-acre donation as an isolated park, conservation officials incorporated it into the surrounding open-space network. Today, visitors can use the fire-road trails to move through the hills, while the undeveloped terrain provides cover and movement routes for wildlife living in the Santa Monica Mountains.A break from developmentThe donation came at a time when undeveloped land in the Hollywood Hills was under pressure from development. Trebek transferred the property to the conservancy rather than retaining it, so it could remain open space.Trebek Open Space now sits beside Runyon Canyon Park, while its trails and surrounding hills form part of the network of open spaces across the Santa Monica Mountains. The MRCA has continued to maintain the property, and agency records show work at Trebek Open Space over the years, including hillside stabilization and vegetation management. For visitors, the property remains a trail area in the Hollywood Hills, and for the wildlife that moves through the surrounding mountains, the land remains undeveloped space between heavily built parts of Los Angeles.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Edouard weakens into a tropical depression after landfall but still dumping rain into Texas
articles.summary: The former Tropical Storm Edouard weakened into a depression while unleashing heavy rains and strong winds on parts of Texas, knocking out power to thousands, toppling trees and flooding roads.
articles.body: PORT ARTHUR, Texas — The former Tropical Storm Edouard weakened into a depression Tuesday night while unleashing heavy rains and strong winds on parts of Texas, knocking out power to thousands, toppling trees and flooding roads. The storm downgraded hours after making landfall near the Texas-Louisiana border with maximum sustained winds of 60 mph (95 kph), according to the National Hurricane Center. Forecasters said the system would keep losing strength as it pushed inland but would likely continue to produce heavy rains and possible flooding into Wednesday. Meanwhile, a burst of tropical weather continued in the Pacific, where three named storms were churning in open waters. The hurricane center expected Edouard to dump 3 to 7 inches (8 to 17 centimeters) of rain with up to 12 inches (30 centimeters) in some areas. Storm makes landfall along Texas-Louisiana line As the center of the storm passed over Beaumont, Texas, about 80 miles (130 kilometers) northeast of Houston, the city’s offices were shuttered and the Texas Office of Emergency Management warned residents to stay off the road. Throughout the city were downed trees blocking roads, traffic signals that weren’t working and flooded underpasses, Beaumont Police said in a post on social media. About 32,000 utility customers were without electricity in Jefferson County, which includes Beaumont, according to poweroutage.com. Mike Gilbert decided ahead of the storm to close his surf shop on Texas’ Crystal Beach because he didn’t want to risk his employees having a difficult time getting home. But, he said, it had ended up just being gray skies and drizzly rain there Tuesday as Edouard made landfall about 60 miles (96 kilometers) northeast of his shop. “You literally never know,” Gilbert said. “It could have all of a sudden moved over 50 miles and picked up 20 mph in wind and it could have been a whole different story.” In Cameron, Louisiana, the winds had picked up by Tuesday morning and rain was coming through on and off, said Connor Salvador, who owns an RV park there near the coast. He said while there could be a “little bit” of flooding if they get a lot of rain, he wasn’t too worried about Edouard. “We’re pretty used to all these types of storms that come through,” he said. Several storms in the Pacific Ocean Forecasters said newly formed Hurricane Lowell in the Pacific Ocean was expected to remain several hundred miles away from Hawaii for the next several days at least, but swells from the hurricane were likely to impact parts of the islands beginning Wednesday. “This hurricane is likely to increase the surf and make for dangerous beach conditions and marine conditions for any boaters near the Hawaiian islands over the next few days,” said Andrew Hagan, a forecaster with the National Hurricane Center. Tropical Storm Marie formed in the Pacific Ocean early Tuesday well offshore of southwest Mexico, the center said. Forecasters said it was expected to become a hurricane by Wednesday night, and swells generated by the storm were expected to affect parts of the coast in southwestern Mexico and the Baja California peninsula over the next few days. Elsewhere in the Pacific, Karina became a hurricane Sunday, fueled by warm waters far from any shore. It strengthened Monday into a powerful Category 4 storm but forecasters said Tuesday that it was expected to weaken.

articles.title: A California man spent nearly 30 years hand-building Salvation Mountain from adobe, straw and thousands of gallons of paint; Leonard Knight’s landmark rises near Niland
articles.summary: US News: Discover the inspiring story of Leonard Knight and his iconic Salvation Mountain, a vibrant testament to faith and art built over 30 years in the California desert. Learn about its rich history, artistic evolution, and preservation efforts.
articles.body: In California’s Imperial Valley, near the community of Niland, a painted mountain rises from the desert with a message at its centre saying, “God Is Love.” Popularly known as Salvation Mountain, the sprawling folk-art environment was created by Leonard Knight, who spent nearly 30 years building, painting, and repeatedly repairing it. In 2014, National Geographic described the structure as a man-made mountain that took 28 years to make, while other contemporary accounts described Knight’s work as a nearly three-decade endeavour.Knight had previously spent years trying to build an enormous hot-air balloon bearing his religious message, but the balloon repeatedly failed to become a workable project. Following his arrival in Southern California in the mid-1980s, Knight eventually brought the idea to the desert near Slab City, and there he started turning the message he had originally hoped to convey through the sky into a monument on the ground. The organisation dedicated to preserving his work dates 1986 as Salvation Mountain’s beginning.Transformation from a small monument to a colourful mountain Leonard Knight did not begin with the giant structure that is visible today. Following the failure of his balloon project, he erected a small monument on a desert ledge using a bucket, a shovel and cement. Knight gradually added cement, sand and discarded materials, thus decorating and expanding the structure with painted designs and his religious message. However, the first version eventually collapsed into a pile of sand, prompting Knight to reevaluate how the mountain should be constructed.According to Salvation Mountain Inc., the organisation dedicated to preserving the mountain, Knight began constructing his second mountain in late 1989, after experimenting with native adobe clay. This time around, he used adobe clay and straw as the principal building materials, producing a sturdier and more solid structure. The resulting mountain ultimately became the basis of the landmark that stands near Niland today.While talking to the publication, National Geographic photographer Aaron Huey recalled meeting Knight when the artist could still carry a 40-pound bucket of adobe up a 30-foot ladder. Knight continued to work slowly and methodically over the years, often continuing repairs as weather damaged sections of the structure. Although his methods were unconventional, they were persistent.Adobe and straw formed the structural basis of the mountain; paint played a huge part in both its appearance and protection. The preservation organisation notes that Knight applied more than ten coats of paint in places, with the layers acting as an additional hardening surface that helped protect the material from cracking. Notably, visitors and supporters donated paint, thus allowing the creator to keep expanding the colourful surface.The current preservation organisation estimates that the site contains more than 100,000 gallons of donated paint, while The Los Angeles Times reported in 2014 that Knight himself generously estimated that he had used more than 500,000 gallons of paint. Although the exact quantity of paint reported over the years varies, it is clear that the mountain was built and maintained with thousands of gallons of donated paint.A sprawling folk-art environmentEventually, the Salvation Mountain became much more than a single painted mound, as the complex now includes the main mountain along with additional structures and artwork. National Geographic described peripheral elements made from telephone poles, tyres, and car windows, along with art cars and sculptures, all decorated with the bright patterns and colourful characteristics of Knight’s work.The mountain’s core message still remains unmistakable, while flowers, waterfalls, birds, hearts, biblical quotations and other spiritual imagery cover the surrounding surfaces. Additionally, the mountain incorporates Knight’s version of the Sinner’s Prayer. It is worth noting that Knight also built structures around the mountain using the same improvised approach he came up with during his second attempt. In 1998, he began constructing a domed Hogan from straw bales and adobe, intending to create a cooler shelter from the desert heat; however, he never moved into the shelter, opting to sleep in his truck. Furthermore, the complex includes a structure called the Museum, which is conceptually based on his earlier hot-air-balloon idea and built with domed areas supported by structures made from tyres, wood and adobe.In 2000, the Fold Art Society of America recorded the Salvation Mountain as a “folk art site worthy of protection,” according to contemporary reports. The Los Angeles Times also reported that Senator Barbara Boxer had later referred to the mountain in the Congressional Record as a national treasure, highlighting the cultural appreciation and recognition for Knight’s work.Leonard Knight’s final yearsContemporary reports described Knight living in the back of a broken-down fire truck without conventional household comforts and spending his days building the mountain, eating, giving tours and talking with visitors. He reportedly regarded the site as a way to communicate his beliefs instead of merely viewing it as a part of an art project.However, as Knight aged, the physical demands became harder to sustain, and by 2011, declining health had forced him into long-term care. Los Angeles Times reported that the creator of Salvation Mountain spent more than two years in a nursing home’s care facility before his death in February 2014 at the age of 82. By then, the structure he had started in the 1980s had become an internationally recognised example of self-taught art, with followers already attempting to preserve his work. After Knight’s death, efforts to preserve the landmark continued, eventually becoming the responsibility of organisations and volunteers dedicated to maintaining his work.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Leadership gaps cloud Pakistan's human rights oversight system
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Pakistan’s human rights oversight framework is facing growing uncertainty as key commissions continue to function without permanent leadership or full.
articles.body: Pakistan’s human rights oversight framework is facing growing uncertainty as key commissions continue to function without permanent leadership or full membership, raising concerns over their independence and effectiveness.The previous National Commission for Human Rights (NCHR) completed its four-year term in November 2025, but a new commission has yet to be fully constituted, news agency ANI cited in its report. The National Commission on the Status of Women (NCSW) is also functioning under an acting chairperson.Former NCHR chairperson Khawar Mumtaz criticised and warned that prolonged reliance on temporary arrangements could weaken the autonomy and performance of independent rights bodies.Human rights activist Peter Jacob said Parliament passed legislation establishing the National Commission for Minorities Rights in December 2025, but appointments to the body remain incomplete.The National Commission on the Rights of the Child has also faced vacancies. The Ministry of Human Rights invited applications in July 2026 for members representing Punjab, Islamabad and Balochistan, The Express Tribune reported.NCHR’s legal status under questionAn amendment to the National Commission for Human Rights Act in 2026 introduced Section 4A, allowing a chairperson to continue for up to 120 days after the expiry of their term or until a successor is appointed.NCHR Chairperson Rabiya Javeri Agha maintained that the commission remains operationally effective, pointing to additional staff recruited two years ago. She said the extension of the chairperson’s tenure was made under the law and reflected practices followed by human rights institutions internationally. Questions regarding the constitution of a new commission, she said, should be directed to the government, according to The Express Tribune.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
